ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Before incorporation, onboarding and each material transaction, identify and document all direct and indirect owners, controllers, directors, authorized signatories, counterparties, banks, freight forwarders and customs representatives. Screen against United Nations Security Council lists, EU restrictive-measures lists, French national restrictions, applicable United States OFAC lists where a US nexus exists, and relevant UK sanctions lists where a UK nexus exists. Apply enhanced due diligence to politically exposed persons, their family members and known close associates under Code monétaire et financier Articles L561-10 and L561-10-1. Verify identity, source of wealth, source of funds, adverse media, ownership chains, country risk, dual-use or controlled-goods exposure, sanctions clauses and payment-route risk. Do not treat a clean automated screening result as conclusive; resolve aliases, transliteration matches and beneficial-ownership ambiguity. File suspicious-transaction reports with TRACFIN where legally required and retain AML records for the statutory period.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Guichet unique des formalités des entreprises operated by the Institut national de la propriété industrielle (INPI), at formalites.entreprises.gouv.fr; legal-registration data are transmitted to the Registre national des entreprises and the competent commercial registry
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: A French SAS name must be stated in the articles and filing in a form accepted by the French registration system. Latin-script names are generally accepted, but the name must be distinctive, not misleading, not contrary to public policy, and not confusingly similar to an existing company, trade name, trademark or domain. Foreign-language wording and transliteration may be used if legally permissible; French legal-form wording or the abbreviation SAS must identify the legal form. Non-Latin characters may create filing, banking and system-compatibility issues and should be accompanied by an exact Latin transliteration. A corporate-name search does not replace trademark, domain-name, trade-name or unfair-competition clearance.
prohibited_and_sensitive_tokens: Organisme public or wording implying a public authority
Any name likely to mislead regarding a regulated activity, official status, geographic origin or relationship with an existing entity
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: France has no general statutory company-name reservation procedure with a standard 30-day reservation period for a SAS. Conduct searches through the INPI databases, Registre national des entreprises, commercial-register sources, EUIPO, INPI trademark records, domain registries and relevant sector registers. Obtain a written pre-clearance or reserve the name contractually only where a filing professional or counterparty offers that service; any contractual reservation period is not a statutory registry right. If the Guichet unique or registry rejects the filing, obtain the rejection reason, correct the articles or name, and resubmit through the portal. For a formal registry decision, use the available administrative or judicial remedy stated in the notification, generally by referral to the competent commercial court for registration matters or by an administrative challenge where the decision is attributable to an administrative authority. Observe the notification deadline, preserve filing evidence and do not commence use of a disputed name while opposition, trademark or unfair-competition risk remains unresolved.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: A SAS must have a registered office in France under Code de commerce Articles L123-11 et seq. A domiciliation company may be used if it is authorized and the domiciliation contract satisfies statutory requirements. A director may, subject to applicable conditions and duration limits, use a personal residence as the registered office. A virtual office is not sufficient by itself for operational substance, customs credibility, banking onboarding, employment, inventory, laboratory, warehouse or regulated activities. For cross-border procurement of battery-grade lithium carbonate, maintain evidence of real management, supplier and customer due diligence, contracts, purchase orders, logistics controls, product classification, customs records, accounting, transfer-pricing support and accessible corporate books. If goods are stored or handled in France, use premises suitable for the activity and assess dangerous-goods, environmental, occupational-safety and transport requirements.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: No reliable public statistical rate exists. Indicative risk assessment: approximately 5% to 15% annual likelihood of an unannounced or short-notice physical verification for a newly incorporated, low-asset SAS with no regulated licence, increasing to approximately 15% to 30% during the first two years where customs, VAT, sanctions, AML, tax, workplace, environmental or product-compliance indicators are present. These are risk estimates, not official probabilities. Maintain a staffed or controlled registered-office capability, current signage or access arrangements where appropriate, complete records and an immediately available legal representative or service provider.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: French Commercial Code (Code de commerce), Articles L.210-1 to L.210-10, L.227-1 to L.227-30 (SAS), and R.123-101 et seq. (RCS filings); general corporate provisions of the Civil Code, Articles 1832 to 1844-17, apply where not disclaimed.
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Guichet unique des formalités des entreprises (single digital portal) and the Registre du commerce et des sociétés (RCS) maintained by the Greffe du tribunal de commerce.
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Statuts de la société (articles of association) and déclaration de constitution (incorporation declaration) submitted through the national Formulaire M0 electronic filing dossier.
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No statutory minimum capital for an SAS; the share capital is freely fixed in the articles. All shares must be subscribed in full. At least 50% of cash contributions must be paid up at incorporation, with the balance payable within five years. Cash subscription funds must be escrowed in a blocked French bank account opened for the company in formation until the RCS registration certificate is issued.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: FIRST WRITTEN RESOLUTION OF THE SOLE SHAREHOLDER ACTING AS CORPORATE BOARD OF [SAS NAME]. Having reviewed the draft French statutes and the share subscription schedule, the undersigned sole shareholder resolves: (1) to subscribe in full the entire nominal share capital of EUR [amount], represented by [number] ordinary shares allotted at par; (2) to deposit and block the cash subscription monies in a French bank account in the name of the company in formation, such funds to be released only after RCS registration; (3) to adopt the final articles of association, including the registered office at [address]; (4) to appoint [Name] as first President, with full powers to bind the company and complete all filings; (5) to authorize the President to publish legal notices and to complete tax, social, customs, and bank formalities. This resolution is recorded in the corporate records.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Drafting and execution of the French SAS articles of association
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Founding shareholders; notary public optional unless a contribution of real property or special asset is made
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Prepare the French-language statuts signed by all shareholders. The articles must state the legal form, duration, company name, registered office, corporate object, share capital, number and nominal value of shares, transfer restrictions, governance rules, and powers of the President. The business object should include wholesale procurement and international distribution of battery-grade lithium carbonate and battery metals. Execute the articles by original signatures and appoint the first President. No notarial act is required for a cash-only SAS.
required_dossiers: Signed draft articles of association
Valid passport or identity card of each shareholder
Proof of residential address of each shareholder (less than 3 months)
Consent of the appointed President to take office
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the registry or a bank queries the articles, execute a supplementary rectifying deed (acte rectificatif) signed by all shareholders and resubmit with the corrected provisions.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Blocking bank deposit of cash capital contributions
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: French commercial bank or Caisse des Dépôts et Consignations
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Open a blocked account (compte bloqué) in the name of the company in formation. Transfer the subscribed cash contributions and obtain a certificate of blocked funds (attestation de blocage des fonds / certificat de dépôt des fonds) stating the company name, deposit date, and amount. The certificate is necessary as proof of capital payment for RCS registration.
required_dossiers: Bank account application form
Draft statutes or subscription schedule showing capital contributions
KYC identification documents for shareholders and beneficial owners
Blocked fund deposit certificate issued by the bank
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the bank requests further beneficial ownership details, provide a corporate structure diagram and signed beneficial ownership declaration. If the blocked amount does not match the articles, correct the contribution schedule or execute a rectification deed before filing.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Publication of the incorporation notice in a legal announcements journal
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Approved legal announcements newspaper (journal d'annonces légales) in the judicial department of the registered office
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Publish an avis de constitution containing the company name, legal form, registered office city, corporate object, share capital, and the RCS city where registration will occur. Ensure the notice is published before submitting the RCS filing. Obtain the attestation de parution from the journal.
required_dossiers: Draft legal announcement text
Signed statutes or an accurate summary
Identified RCS registration city
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the publication notice is rejected or contains inaccurate information, publish a corrected notice in the same or another approved journal and obtain a new attestation de parution.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Electronic submission of the incorporation dossier to the single formalities portal
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Guichet unique des formalités des entreprises (formalites.entreprises.gouv.fr), acting for the Greffe du tribunal de commerce
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Create an account on the official portal and submit the creation application for a legal entity. Provide company data equivalent to Formulaire M0, attach the signed statutes, legal announcement certificate, blocked funds certificate, registered-office occupancy proof, President identification and acceptance, beneficial ownership declaration, and any auditor documents if applicable. Pay the official registry fee upon submission.
required_dossiers: Completed electronic incorporation form (M0 data)
Signed statutes
Attestation de parution from the legal announcements journal
Certificate of blocked funds issued by the bank
Proof of registered-office occupancy
President's identity document and signed acceptance of office
Beneficial ownership declaration
Statutory auditor acceptance, if a financial controller is required
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the portal issues a query, amend and resubmit the deficient documents within 15 business days of the invitation. If the RCS registry formally objects, file a supplementary response through the portal and, if rejected, refile the corrected dossier after resolving the stated legal impediment.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: RCS examination, registration, and issuance of the Kbis extract
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Greffe du tribunal de commerce, Registre du commerce et des sociétés
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: The registry verifies the legal form, corporate object, capital rules, and compliance of signatures. Upon approval, it assigns the RCS registration number, transmits data to INSEE for SIREN, SIRET, and APE code allocation, and to the DGFiP for tax registration. The official extract of the registration is the extrait Kbis.
required_dossiers: No additional applicant action; the registry completes the procedure from the submitted portal file
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the registry rejects the name due to prior intellectual property or corporate name conflict, adopt a distinctive alternative name by shareholder resolution and resubmit. If the file is queried for formal omissions, provide the requested certificate within the official cure period; after final refusal, a new dossier and applicable fee may be required.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Post-registration tax, customs, and bank activation formalities
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: DGFiP / Service des impôts des entreprises; Direction générale des douanes et droits indirects for customs; commercial bank
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: After receiving the extrait Kbis, verify the automatic allocation of a French value-added tax registration number. If a VAT number has not been issued, apply to the competent SIE. Submit an EORI number application if importing or exporting outside the European Union. Open or convert the operational corporate bank account using the Kbis and finalize the internal corporate records with signed appointment documents.
required_dossiers: Extrait Kbis
Signed statutes
Identity documents of officers
EORI application and customs statement if cross-border trade occurs
Proof of registered office and bank signatory mandate
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the VAT number is not granted or delayed, file a written request with the SIE providing the Kbis and articles. If customs queries the EORI application, correct the legal representative or address details and resubmit through the customs portal.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Not applicable for the registered wholesale activity; would be DREAL only if the company later establishes an industrial installation subject to the ICPE regime.
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: No separate operating license is required; the extrait Kbis confirming RCS registration constitutes the valid commercial trading licence. The activity is a wholesale procurement and distribution operation under ISIC 4662, not a manufacturing or chemical production facility.

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: DREAL (Direction régionale de l'environnement, de l'aménagement et du logement)
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Exempt — no EIA or ICPE registration is triggered by the pure trading/brokerage activity. Future storage or handling of lithium carbonate above applicable thresholds would require a separate assessment under the Code de l'environnement.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: No specific wastewater, VOC, or waste-disposal thresholds apply at registration. If material handling or repackaging begins, the company must comply with REACH and CLP transport and labeling rules, keep lithium carbonate dry and contained, avoid dust releases, and follow Code de l'environnement obligations for any wastewater discharge or waste tracking.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: No fire brigade approval or civil-defense clearance is required for a purely administrative and commercial operation. Office and warehouse premises must nevertheless satisfy municipal building codes, fire-safety means of escape, and Code du travail occupational health and safety duties. If a physical warehouse is opened, further fire-prevention review and building load verification may be required by the local zoning and fire authority.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Direction générale des Finances publiques (DGFiP), through the official impots.gouv.fr portal. VAT registrations and filings for foreign businesses are handled by the Service des impôts des entreprises étrangères (SIEE).
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: A French SAS is registered for tax purposes through its business formalities filing via the competent Guichet unique operated by the Institut national de la propriété industrielle (INPI); registration results in allocation of a SIREN and establishment-specific SIRET, and the company obtains its French VAT number from DGFiP when VAT registration is required. A foreign entity making taxable supplies in France must apply to the SIEE for French VAT registration before commencing those supplies, provide its formation and tax-registration documents, identify its French activities and expected transactions, and appoint a French fiscal representative if required. Non-EU entities generally must appoint a fiscal representative unless an applicable mutual-assistance arrangement provides an exemption. VAT registration is conducted through the applicable DGFiP process; the VAT number is generally FR plus a two-character key and the entity's SIREN.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: A French SAS is ordinarily subject to French corporate income tax (impôt sur les sociétés, IS). It may elect temporary taxation under the personal income tax rules under Article 239 bis AB of the French Tax Code if the statutory conditions are met, including qualifying ownership, size, age, and business-activity conditions; the election is limited to five fiscal years and is not a US-style check-the-box election. No general check-the-box or elective hybrid-mismatch classification regime applies. French tax residence and source rules determine the taxable scope; the French territorial system does not itself make a SAS tax-exempt.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: Value Added Tax (VAT; taxe sur la valeur ajoutée, TVA), under French and EU VAT rules.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: For a French-established business, the domestic small-business VAT exemption (franchise en base) generally uses annual turnover thresholds of EUR 85,000 for supplies of goods and certain accommodation or food activities and EUR 37,500 for services, subject to statutory rules and applicable threshold changes. These are exemption thresholds, not a general VAT-registration threshold. A non-established business making taxable supplies in France generally has no domestic turnover threshold and must register when required under the applicable place-of-supply and reverse-charge rules. The EU-wide threshold for qualifying cross-border intra-Community distance sales and certain electronic services is EUR 10,000, subject to the relevant EU rules.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: France is introducing mandatory domestic B2B electronic invoicing and transaction e-reporting in phases. From 1 September 2026, all businesses must be able to receive e-invoices; issuance obligations begin on that date for large and intermediate-sized businesses and generally on 1 September 2027 for small and medium-sized businesses. Covered invoices must use a compliant format and be transmitted through a DGFiP-authorized partner dematerialization platform (plateforme de dématérialisation partenaire, PDP), directly or through the public invoicing portal where available. Relevant transaction and payment data must be reported under the e-reporting rules. France does not generally require real-time pre-clearance or digital tax stamping of each VAT invoice.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Exports of goods dispatched or transported from France to a destination outside the EU may be exempt from French VAT with a right to deduct input VAT, provided the supplier can substantiate export and meet the statutory conditions, including the applicable time limit for export and evidence of exit from the EU customs territory. Intra-Community supplies are subject to separate exemption rules, including a valid customer VAT number and proof of transport. Services are not automatically zero-rated because a customer is offshore; their VAT treatment depends on place-of-supply rules, customer status, and any applicable exemption. For B2B services supplied to a taxable customer established outside France, the general place-of-supply rule commonly places taxation where the customer is established, subject to exceptions.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Export customs declaration with the Movement Reference Number (MRN) and customs confirmation of exit from the EU
Commercial invoice identifying the goods, buyer, destination, and applicable VAT-exemption basis
Transport evidence appropriate to the mode of shipment, such as bill of lading, air waybill, CMR, or carrier delivery confirmation
Purchase order, sales contract, delivery records, and evidence linking the exported goods to the relevant invoice
Proof of payment or settlement records where available; France does not impose a general inward-remittance certificate requirement for export VAT exemption
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: France has no general statutory foreign-exchange repatriation deadline for export proceeds. The supplier must retain sufficient evidence that the goods left the EU and that the transaction qualifies for exemption. Unsupported or incorrectly claimed export exemption may result in reassessment of output VAT, late-payment interest, and tax penalties; penalties depend on the nature and degree of fault and may be increased for deliberate conduct or fraudulent manoeuvres. Input VAT refunds may be denied or recovered where entitlement or supporting evidence is insufficient. Customs, VAT, and accounting records should be retained for the applicable statutory periods.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Banque de France (BdF) acting within the Eurosystem, with delegated authority from the French Treasury (Direction Générale du Trésor, Ministry of Economy, Finance and Industrial and Digital Sovereignty) for external financial relations, balance-of-payments statistics and cross-border payment surveillance. The ACPR (Autorité de Contrôle Prudentiel et de Résolution) supervises licensed banks and e-money institutions; the Banque de France operates the foreign-exchange information system and the SARFT-style reporting portal for cross-border fund movements.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: The French franc legacy controls have been superseded by the euro regime, which is fully convertible under Article 63 TFEU and the OECD Codes of Liberalisation. France applies no material exchange-control restrictions to current-account trade payments for battery-grade lithium carbonate imports; the capital account is likewise liberalized for EU and third-country investors, with no prior authorization required for non-sensitive wholesale distribution activities. Profit remittance of dividends to non-resident shareholders is unrestricted from a treasury perspective; any levy (e.g., 30% flat tax or treaty-reduced withholding) is a fiscal matter and not a liquidity-clearing constraint. The only compliance layer is statistical: cross-border transactions are automatically reported to the Banque de France by the instructing bank for balance-of-payments purposes, and foreign direct investment inflows (≥10% voting rights in the SAS) trigger a mandatory 'Investment in France' external-finance notification (déclaration d'investissement direct étranger en France) within 20 days of the operation.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: France does not impose any statutory surrender timeline, mandatory conversion ratio, or repatriation quota on export proceeds; a French resident company may lawfully retain export receivables in EUR or convertible foreign currency. The only regulatory obligations are (i) routing all export receipts through an authorised bank, (ii) accurate encoding of the transaction for the Banque de France balance-of-payments return, and (iii) declaration of foreign commercial debt (dette extérieure) when the outstanding balance of supplier credits or advances granted by non-residents exceeds the regulatory notification threshold (absolutely €1.0 million) on a monthly basis. The subject SAS is an importer of lithium carbonate; hence the export-surrender dimension is not applicable to its primary procurement flows.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Capital Escrow Account (compte de dépôt de capital) and Operational Account (compte courant d'exploitation)
Operational Account and Trade Finance Account (LC/MT700 issuance line)

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.bank_name: Crédit Agricole Corporate and Investment Bank (Crédit Agricole CIB) / LCL
tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Capital Escrow Account and Commodity-Focused Operational Account
Operational Account and Structured Metals Trade Finance Account
Operational Account for euro-denominated Treasury Settlement

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Feasibility rating: Medium for domestic euro payments and administrative treasury, but Low for cross-border documentary trade flows. A French ACPR-licensed Electronic Money Institution (e.g., Qonto, Treezor, Mangopay) may lawfully open a payment account for the SAS, issue IBANs, execute SEPA and SWIFT MT103 transactions, and provide expense-card infrastructure; however, an EMI is prohibited from extending credit, granting overdrafts, issuing commercial letters of credit (MT700), or providing trade-finance instruments. A non-EU offshore EMI without a French passport or an ACPR branch licence has no legal standing to maintain an operational payment account for a French resident SAS under PSD2 and could not serve the cross-border procurement rails of battery-grade lithium carbonate. The recommended structure is therefore a full-service commercial bank for primary clearing, with an EMI optionally layered for FX card and payroll services.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Remote corporate account opening is recognised in French law via eIDAS-qualified electronic signatures, videoconference identity verification, and dematerialised K-Bis (registre du commerce) extraction. In practice, however, a battery-metals arbitrage SAS with non-resident UBOs is categorised as Medium_Risk_Enhanced, and French tier-1 banks require an enhanced due diligence interview: at least one legal representative must attend an in-person or high-grade video 'entretien de conformité' with the compliance officer; fully digital opening is usually accepted only by neo-banks and not by the commodity trade-finance desks. The repository bundle comprises the original signed statutes, K-Bis, declaration of effective beneficiaries filed with the commercial registry, directors' passports plus proof of address, and, for a non-EU resident director, a police/penal-record extract or bank reference letter when the bank's risk appetite so requires.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Persistent high-value SWIFT wires to suppliers domiciled in the People's Republic of China or Hong Kong SAR for lithium carbonate consignments, raising screening flags for sanctions-circumvention, trade-based money laundering, and opaque beneficial ownership.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Complete trade-chain file: notarised commercial contract with Incoterms (CIF Shanghai or FOB Shenzhen), supplier's business-registry extract, export licence references, supplier's certificate of origin (battery-grade Li2CO3, HS code 2836.91.00), original bills of lading, customs import Summary Declaration (ENS), DEB/Douane entries, quality certificate from an independent assay laboratory, and a signed end-user undertaking confirming the goods are non-military battery material.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Advance payment demands exceeding 50% of the purchase order value under an open-account wire structure to a recently incorporated overseas entity.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Minutes of the shareholders' meeting authorising treasury payment, invoice and pro-forma invoice reconciliation memo, supplier's documentary bank guarantee or standby LC issued by a prime bank, historical settlement statements proving a two-year performance track record, and a group treasury policy letter confirming that open-account exposure to third-party suppliers is capped by a board-approved limit.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: UBO profile showing tax residence in a non-EU jurisdiction, recent incorporation sequence, or mismatch between declared wealth and the value of paid-up capital contributed to the SAS.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Trade-registry beneficial-ownership declaration (Déclaration des Bénéficiaires Effectifs), extracts of identity documents with certified apostille translation, 12-month source-of-funds bank statements for each contributing UBO, tax authority residence certificates, affidavit of independent wealth, and a legal counsel comfort letter confirming the capital contribution complies with French monetary and financial provisions.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Sector-specific ESG provenance protest: banks conducting commodity-lending due diligence demand 'responsible minerals' assurance for lithium sourced from Argentina, Chile, or Australia, and refuse financing absent a verifiable environmental and social audit trail.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Responsible-Sourcing Policy signed by the SAS director, CMRT/RMI form where applicable, original mining-country certificate of origin, ESG audit report of the upstream supplier (ISO 14001 or equivalent), logistics-chain continuity plan, and a legal opinion confirming the product is outside the EU Conflict Minerals Regulation scope.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: The non-EU shareholder invests into the SAS through a SWIFT MT103 wire to the BNP Paribas or Société Générale account with purpose code 'CAPITAL INCREASE / FONDS PROPRES' and reference to the shareholders' resolution. The bank encodes the inflow as euro-area external liability in the Banque de France balance-of-payments return; for a foreign direct investment involving ≥10% of the capital or voting rights, the company must deliver the 'Investment in France' declaration (DIDE) to the Banque de France within 20 working days. Capital must be credited as paid-in capital and shown in the corporate accounts under 'Capital social' to prevent recharacterisation as shareholder debt; the bank's credit advice should be preserved as the treasury evidence of the contribution. If the contribution is made in foreign currency, the French receiving bank converts it at the ECB fixing applied to the account contract; any settlement-risk protection requires the SWIFT ordering bank to use a direct correspondent of the French beneficiary institution.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: For the purchase of battery-grade lithium carbonate powder from China, the recommended clearing rail is an irrevocable documentary letter of credit: the French issuing bank (e.g., Société Générale or BNP Paribas) transmits a SWIFT MT700 through its China correspondent to the supplier's advising bank, with settlement at sight against compliant presentation (commercial invoice, full-set original ocean bill of lading, certificate of quality attesting to purity ≥99.5% Li₂CO₃, packing list, rules of origin certificate). Where open-account settlement is commercially necessary, the company instructs a SWIFT MT103 with purpose code 'IMPORT GOODS / METALS AND MINERAL WHOLESALE' and a precise payment narrative matching the customs import declaration; all such payments must be routed through the French bank's compliance-approved trade desk, with invoice, bill of lading, and customs entry attached as supporting evidence inside the bank's trade surveillance system. SEPA Credit Transfer is available only for intra-EEA euro supplier payments and is not applicable to Chinese counterparties.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: EUR/USD deliverable FX forward contracts (ISDA 2002 French Master Agreement, EMIR-cleared where required; actual physical delivery of EUR and USD at maturity).
FX swaps (Cambiste deposits/reverse deposits or classic swap-cambiste) for short-term treasury liquidity management up to 12 months.
Cross-currency interest rate swaps (CCS/CRS) to fix EUR-USD conversion costs on medium-term supplier credit lines or trade payables.
Vanilla EUR/USD option strategies — bought calls, collars, and zero-premium risk reversals to cap USD depreciation against the euro without speculative features.
FX spot forward conversion lines under the bank's daily treasury facility, including standing instruction hedging for monthly trade settlements.

NDFs are permissible only for the non-euro trading currencies of the underlying supply chain (e.g., USD/CNY or USD/CLP) where the local currency has no deliverability; NDF contracts with a euro leg are not accepted by French credit institutions because the euro is freely deliverable and such contracts would constitute non-genuine risk-only instruments.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Filing of annual corporate income tax return and supporting schedules (Déclaration de résultats, Form 2065-SD with 2058-series annexes and simplified balance sheet schedules)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Calendar-year-end entities: by 3 May of the following year (next business day if 3 May is non-working); non-calendar-year fiscal year-end: within three months after the close of the fiscal year.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late-filing surcharge of 10% on assessed corporation tax, plus late-payment interest at 0.2% per month; a further 40% penalty may apply for deliberate failure; persistent tax enforcement may lead to seizure of assets and, ultimately, court-ordered insolvency and RCS strike-off.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Deposit of annual financial statements at the commercial registry (dépôt des comptes annuels au registre du commerce et des sociétés)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Greffe du Tribunal de Commerce / Registre du Commerce et des Sociétés via INPI Guichet Unique
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within one month after the shareholders' ordinary meeting approving the annual accounts, and in all cases within seven months of fiscal year-end; extension may be granted by the President of the Commercial Court upon reasoned request.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Formal notice to regularise within 30 days; fine of up to EUR 1,500 per late filing; continuing default exposes the company to a judicial appearance and, after due procedure, administrative radiation (strike-off) from the RCS.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual ordinary shareholders' approval of annual accounts and allocation of profit (assemblée générale ordinaire / décision de l'associé unique)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Internal corporate minute book (Registre des décisions); the approved accounts are subsequently filed with the RCS and the tax authorities
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Must be held within six months of the end of the fiscal year; the Commercial Court may grant an extension.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: No immediate pecuniary penalty, but failure to approve accounts blocks lawful dividend distribution, exposes the president to civil liability for losses, and may allow the court to compel a meeting or the compulsory appointment of an auditor.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: A statutory auditor (commissaire aux comptes) is mandatory for an SAS when, at the balance-sheet date, at least two of the following three thresholds are exceeded for either of the two preceding fiscal years: total balance sheet above EUR 4,000,000; net turnover above EUR 8,000,000; average workforce above 50 employees. An auditor may also be required by statutory groups, regulated activities, or shareholder request.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: French local GAAP under the Plan Comptable Général (PCG) and Code de commerce; IFRS is not permitted for standalone non-listed SAS individual annual accounts unless otherwise required by law.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: France does not impose a calendar-based annual UBO confirmation. The beneficial-owner declaration (Déclaration des bénéficiaires effectifs) is submitted on incorporation and must be updated within 30 days of any relevant change in effective ownership, including SAS share transfers. The annual compliance process must verify that the RCS beneficial-owner record and the share-transfer register remain aligned after any transfer.
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Registre des décisions de l'associé unique or des assemblées générales (decision register/minute book)
Registre des mouvements de titres (share register and share-transfer register)
Registre de présence / procès-verbaux of shareholders' meetings

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: EUR 150 – EUR 1,000 (approx. USD 165 – USD 1,100) per year depending on domiciliation offering and region
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: No compulsory audit fee where statutory audit thresholds are not met; if an audit is required or voluntarily engaged, typical fee for a small import/trading SAS is EUR 4,000 – EUR 12,000 (approx. USD 4,400 – USD 13,200).

corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: Reduced 15% CIT rate on the first EUR 42,500 of taxable income for qualifying SMEs generating turnover below EUR 10 million; research tax credit (CIR) at 30% of eligible R&D expenditure; additional 3.3% social contribution on corporate income tax exceeding EUR 763,000; no broad tax holidays for pure trading vehicles.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Déclaration de résultats 2065-SD (CIT return) with annexes 2052 to 2059-SD; filed electronically via the EDI-TDFC module on impots.gouv.fr.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.reporting_frequency: Annual; four quarterly CIT advance payments (acomptes) due in March, June, September and December, with final settlement at filing.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: For fiscal years ending on 31 December, the return must be filed by the third business day after 1 May; for other fiscal year-ends, the return must be filed within three months of the accounting closing date.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Legal identification: registered name, SIREN/SIRET number, corporate form (SAS), registered office address, and fiscal year opening/closing dates.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-resident entity with a French permanent establishment (PE) must disclose the PE's French address and foreign company registration; if no PE exists, no 2065-SD return is normally required.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Net turnover excluding VAT, including sales of battery-grade lithium carbonate, procurement margins, commissions, and other operating revenue classified under the APE/NAF code.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Report only turnover attributable to the French PE or the French SAS; cross-border intercompany sales must be allocated in line with transfer pricing documentation.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Pre-tax book profit or loss determined under French accounting standards (PCG), after depreciation, provisions, and valuation adjustments.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-resident taxpayers with a PE must present French books maintained in accordance with local GAAP and apply fiscal adjustments under Article 209 CGI.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Tax loss carryforward position: prior-year losses available for set-off and the portion deducted against current-year taxable income.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: The PE may deduct loss carryforwards related to French-source activity, subject to proof of the loss and statutory limiting rules (EUR 1 million plus 50% of excess or the relevant carryforward window).

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Net taxable result after loss carryforwards and special deductions, subject to CIT at 25%; indicates eligibility for the reduced 15% SME rate.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-resident entities generally cannot access the 15% SME reduced rate unless the PE operates as a qualifying small enterprise; otherwise apply 25% plus 3.3% social contribution if the tax exceeds EUR 763,000.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Tax credits such as research tax credit (CIR), innovation tax credit (CII), and foreign tax credits.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: The PE may claim credits only for French-eligible expenditure; attach treaty articles and foreign residence certificates where a foreign tax credit is claimed.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing penalty: 10% of the tax due if no formal notice; 20% after a 30-day formal notice; 40% in cases of intentional omission; 80% for fraudulent maneuvers. Late payment interest accrues at 0.20% per month, and an additional 5% late-payment surcharge applies if tax is paid after the due date.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 25% for non-resident corporate shareholders; 30% for non-resident individuals (12.8% income tax plus 17.2% social levies), before any treaty reduction.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: To claim double tax treaty relief, the beneficial owner must provide a valid tax residence certificate, generally Form 5000, to the French paying agent before distribution. The French administration may issue an advance notice enabling reduced or nil withholding at source. Where tax is nevertheless withheld, the non-resident must file a refund claim using Form 5001/5002 with the competent French tax office, within the statutory claim window. The EU Parent-Subsidiary Directive may also eliminate withholding for qualifying EU corporate shareholders holding the required participation for two years.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Statutory withholding on royalties paid to non-residents is 33.33%; domestic law generally imposes no withholding on arm's-length interest paid to corporate non-residents. DTA rates commonly reduce royalties to 0% or 10% and interest to 0% or 10%; the EU Interest and Royalties Directive may provide 0% between associated companies.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: EUR 400 million (annual turnover or total assets of the French entity, or of the consolidated group to which it belongs)
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: France does not apply UAE-style Economic Substance Regulations, but enforces economic substance through the substance-over-form principle, the General Anti-Abuse Rule (abus de droit under Article L.64 LPF), and BEPS-related principal purpose tests. A French SAS carrying on battery-grade lithium carbonate procurement must maintain genuine substance — real employees, physical premises, and actual commercial decision-making — to sustain tax residence, support permanent establishment allocation, and preserve treaty benefits. Artificial or conduit structures lacking commercial reality are recharacterized and denied tax benefits.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Deliberately omitting sales and revenue from the 2065-SD return, hiding bank accounts, or failing to register the SAS as a CIT taxpayer while conducting real commercial activity in France.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Under Article 1741 CGI, tax fraud is punishable by up to five years' imprisonment and a fine of EUR 75,000; aggravated circumstances carry increased penalties. Tax authorities may reassess profit with a 40% bad-faith penalty plus late-payment interest at 0.20% per month.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: A director, whether de jure or de facto, may be prosecuted personally; the corporate veil can be pierced through civil liability for unlawful management (action en comblement du passif), and courts may impose travel restrictions, asset freezes, and confiscation of personal property.
